The execution chain (Tool Runtime → Permission Decision → sandbox → side effects) solves "how to act, how to be constrained." It turns "the model wants to act" into "actually executing within controlled boundaries." The task chain (Task Runtime) solves "how to run concurrently, how to persist, how to flow back." It makes background tasks, sub-agents, and remote execution share the same lifecycle management, without reinventing state management for each scenario. The extension layer (MCP/Skills/Plugins) is not a fourth isolated chain; it injects capabilities into the three main chains, while adhering to "external chaos is fine, internal must converge"—external sources are uniformly translated into internal objects, and the system internally speaks only one language.
